  string(REPLACE "/INCREMENTAL" "" CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_DEBUG  "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_DEBUG}")
endif()


# === ПОСТРОИТЬ КОМАНДЫ КОМПИЛЯЦИИ И ЛИНКА ===
function(configure_target trgt PRODUCT_TARGET)
if(MSVC)
  # минимальная поддерживаемая ОС - win7 (и все дальнейшие)
  target_compile_definitions(${trgt} PRIVATE _WIN32_WINNT=0x0601)
  # в msvc /Zi, /EHsc, /DEBUG  будут дублироваться, но прописываются для ясности
  # target_compile_options - произвольные флаги компилятора 
  # PRIVATE даёт нетранзитивность: А (этот объект) и Б к нему сможет линковаться. а когда К линк. к Б, то К не будет линк. к А
  target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:/EHsc> /W4 /permissive-)

  # сюда будет заходить только для программ из задач, не для программ для тестирования (run_case, check) - им эти флаги не нужны
  if(PRODUCT_TARGET)
    # CMake проставит след. флаги автоматиечки: /Od /O2; /MDd /MD; /DNDEBUG
    target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>:/Zi /fsanitize=address> $<$<CONFIG:Release>:/Zi>)
    target_link_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>:/DEBUG> $<$<CONFIG:Release>:/DEBUG /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF>)
  endif()

else()
  target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  # и в ветке продуктов, и в ветке тестовых программ оптимизация на релизе будет именно -O2, а не cmake-default -O3
  if (PRODUCT_TARGET) 
    # -O0 на дебаге будет подтянут CMake автоматически, а на релизе -DNDEBUG
    target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>: -g -fsanitize=address> $<$<CONFIG:Release>: -g -O2>)
    target_link_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>: -fsanitize=address>)
  else()
    target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Release>: -O2>)
  endif()
endif()
endfunction()


# === Ф-ЦИЯ ДОБАВЛЕНИЯ ЗАДАЧИ === 
# сборки exe из main.c/main.cpp; уходит в каталог build/cfg/dir
function(add_task dir trgt src lib)
  # добавление исполняемного файла 
  # цель и её исходник. цель имеет одно имя (логическое, типа t1_c), а сделанный ею файл - другое (OUTPUT_NAME main)
  add_executable(${trgt} ${src})

  # в CMAKE_BINARY_DIR будет тот каталог, который был передан по -B
  set_target_properties(${trgt} PROPERTIES
  OUTPUT_NAME main
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${dir})

  # с кем линкуемся
  # тут private не имеет смысла (.exe конечен, к нему не линкуются), просто для единообразия
  target_link_libraries(${trgt} PRIVATE ${lib})

  # определение типа библиотеки т.к. на windows для .dll нужно доп. действие для связки с .exe
  get_target_property(lib_type ${lib} TYPE)
  # копирование dll в папку к exe даже если сам exe не перестраивался
  if(WIN32 AND lib_type STREQUAL "SHARED_LIBRARY")
    set(copied_dll "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${dir}/${lib}.dll")
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${copied_dll}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different $<TARGET_FILE:${lib}> "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${dir}"
      DEPENDS ${lib} 
      COMMENT "Copying DLL ${lib} next to ${trgt}"
      VERBATIM)
    add_custom_target(${trgt}_dll DEPENDS "${copied_dll}")
    add_dependencies(${trgt} ${trgt}_dll)
  endif()

  # команда для cl+link. флаг PRODUCT_TARGET = ON - т.е. пойдём по ветке if (PRODUCT_TARGET) с флагами для программ-задач
  configure_target(${trgt} ON)
 
endfunction()

# генерация version.h из шаблона
# @PROJECT_VERSION@ подставится реальная версия из project(VERSION)
# @ONLY - подставляются только @VAR@, а не ${...} (в шаблоне только @PROJECT_VERSION@). для защиты

# ф-ция cреза всего после major_minor: "19.51.36247.0" -> "19.51"; "4.3.1-msvc1" -> "4.3"; "1.13.2" -> "1.13"
function(to_major_minor out in)

  set(${out} "${matched}" PARENT_SCOPE)
endfunction()

# версия компонента проверяется и происходит падение/предупреждение/сообщение в зависимости от версии
function(check_component name actual tested min)
  if(NOT min STREQUAL "0" AND actual VERSION_LESS min)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "${name} ${actual} is older than minimal ${min}. upgrade the version")
  else()
    list(FIND tested "${actual}" _tested_idx)
    if(NOT _tested_idx EQUAL -1)
      # когда actual входит в список проверенных
      message(STATUS "${name} ${actual} is one of tested ${tested}")
    else()
      message(WARNING "${name} ${actual} is not one of tested ${tested}")
    endif()
  endif()
endfunction()

Now review. Key issues:

1. **Coverage tool version check not added** to toolchain_versions.cmake / root. They added `find_program` but no version check. They asked "флаги и проверку компонента" — check_component for coverage missing. Also the message is two adjacent string literals in `message(FATAL_ERROR "..." "...")` — CMake concatenates them without space/newline: "found.Install". Actually CMake `message` takes multiple args and concatenates them with no separator. So the message will be "wasnt found.Install it and build again". Need a space or single string. Minor.

2. **`find_program` cache poisoning / PATH**: `find_program(MICROSOFT_COVERAGE NAMES Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console)` — this caches the result. If run from a normal shell where not on PATH, it fails; docs say use Developer/Native prompt. Their environment: `where.exe` found it, maybe because PowerShell session has it. Need to test in actual Native Tools prompt. The plan says build from Native Tools anyway. But `find_program` is only executed when CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is Coverage; if the cache was configured without it, no issue. However, if a user first configures Debug, then switches to Coverage in the same build dir (not possible with presets—separate dirs), find_program runs. Fine.
   - More important: `find_program` result is cached in CMakeCache. If the tool later disappears, cache still points to nonexistent path; `if(NOT MICROSOFT_COVERAGE)` passes because cache has stale value. Could add `if(NOT EXISTS "${MICROSOFT_COVERAGE}")`. Minor robustness.
   - Name: `MICROSOFT_COVERAGE` is vague; maybe `COVERAGE_CONSOLE`. Not important.
   - Version check: run `--version`, parse `18.7.0-preview...`, `to_major_minor` → 18.7; add `TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_TESTED "18.7"`? The tool version is tied to VS; might be 18.x. Since they test on 18.7, set tested 18.7, min maybe 17.2? But Build Tools 2026 is 18.x. The course says VS 2026. For C++ static support 17.2; dynamic existed earlier. Min could be 17.2, but their project supports VS 2026. Simpler: tested 18.7, min "0" or "17.2". Need to discuss. But the user asked to check; I should point out missing version check.
   - Also README versions table not updated (not in diff). Point out.

3. **Flags set unconditionally**: `set(CMAKE_*_FLAGS_COVERAGE ... CACHE ... FORCE)` is executed for **every** configuration, including Debug/Release. It doesn't affect Debug/Release because the variables are only used when CONFIG=Coverage. So harmless, but it forces cache entries in debug/release build dirs too. Not a functional bug. However, **`CACHE ... FORCE` on every configure** means if someone manually edits the cache value for coverage, it gets overwritten. Acceptable (single source of truth). But there's a subtle issue: `CMAKE_C_FLAGS_COVERAGE` with `/DNDEBUG` and `/MD`? They didn't include `/MD`. CMake's default `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY` is `MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>DLL`, so Coverage → `/MD`. Good. But is that guaranteed? `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY` default is set by CMake; yes, non-Debug gets `/MD`. Fine. No `/MD` needed.
   - They didn't add `/EHsc`? It's added in `configure_target` for C++ targets (`$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:/EHsc>`). Tests use `configure_target(... OFF)`, but the `/EHsc` line is outside `if(PRODUCT_TARGET)`, so all targets get it. Good.
   - They didn't add `-O2` for GCC Coverage; the `else()` branch has `$<CONFIG:Release>` only; Coverage on Linux is fatal earlier (non-MSVC FATAL_ERROR). So no issue now. But the `else()` FATAL_ERROR is inside `if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Coverage") if(MSVC) ... else() FATAL_ERROR`. On Linux Coverage config, it fails. Good.
   - **Ordering issue**: The Coverage check (`if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Coverage")`) is **before** the default `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` assignment (lines 174-176). If no `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` is set (defaults to Debug), fine. If preset sets Coverage, fine. But if someone configures with `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Coverage`, fine. No issue. However, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` may be empty in multi-config; not relevant (Ninja).
   - The check runs **before** `project()`? Let's see: the coverage check is inserted at line ~145, after `project()` at line 74. So compiler is already detected. Good. But `find_program` for the tool before `project()` would also work. Fine.
   - **Fatal error on non-Windows** uses `if(MSVC)` not `if(WIN32)`. On Windows with clang-cl, MSVC variable false → "no coverage build for non-Windows OS" incorrect message. Not current scope (only MSVC/GCC). Could use `if(WIN32)` and then `if(MSVC)`. Minor.

4. **The `/DEBUG` linker flags**: `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_COVERAGE` and `CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS_COVERAGE` set. But for static libraries? No linker. For DLL import libs? Shared linker covers. Good. However, CMake may also need `CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS_COVERAGE`? No modules. Fine.
   - `/DEBUG` in Release? Their configure_target already adds `/DEBUG` for Release. For Coverage, global linker flags add it for all targets including tests. Good.
   - **PDB generation for compile**: `/Zi` in compile flags; CMake's `TARGET_COMPILE_PDB` and `/Fd`? With `/Zi`, CMake typically passes `/Fd` per target? Earlier build.ninja showed `TARGET_COMPILE_PDB` but no `/Fd` in the FLAGS line. Maybe CMake passes `-Fd` via a separate part? Let me check the actual compile rule. If `/Fd` is not passed, all targets share `vc140.pdb` (as in Makefile era). With Ninja parallel, multiple cl writing same PDB could conflict or lose debug info. Their current Debug/Release builds already use `/Zi` and presumably work; CMake may set `/Fd` via `CMAKE_PDB_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`? Let's inspect build.ninja for `/Fd` explicitly (earlier grep `/Fd` returned none, only `/Zi`). Hmm, earlier grep pattern `/Fd|/Zi|pdb` returned lines with `/Zi` but no `/Fd`; maybe CMake uses `/Fd` in the rule as `$TARGET_COMPILE_PDB`? Let me check the rule definition. This matters for coverage PDB quality. But it's existing behavior, not introduced by their change. Still, coverage relies on PDBs. If Debug/Release currently produce `main.pdb` and work, likely CMake handles it. Let me inspect `build.ninja` for `TARGET_COMPILE_PDB` usage and `vc140.pdb` files. Read-only.
   - Actually CMake sets `TARGET_COMPILE_PDB` property but may not use it unless `COMPILE_PDB_NAME`; with MSVC, CMake's default `CMAKE_COMPILE_PDB_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` is empty; `TARGET_COMPILE_PDB` is a property used for install? The compile command may include `/Fd` only if `COMPILE_PDB_NAME` set. Their build might indeed write `vc140.pdb` in build root. Let me check files. If `vc140.pdb` exists in build/debug, then all targets share it; with Ninja parallel, cl may conflict, but they've built with `-j` successfully? Earlier they had `/Fd` discussions in Makefile era; with CMake maybe `/FS`? Let me check. This is tangential but relevant to coverage symbol quality.
   - Also note: coverage needs linker PDB, which is generated with `/DEBUG`; `main.pdb` exists. Even if compile PDBs are shared, linker can read them. But if `vc140.pdb` gets overwritten by another target, symbols for earlier objects may be lost → coverage mapping holes. This is a real risk. Their plan should verify PDBs. But the user asked only review of their changes; I can mention as a risk to check in probe, not a defect of the change.

5. **`CMAKE_C_FLAGS_COVERAGE` uses `CACHE ... FORCE` without a guard**: It overwrites user-provided flags. For a training project, fine, but note.
   - It doesn't include `/MD`; CMake default gives `/MD` for Coverage. Verify with `ninja -t commands`.
   - It doesn't include `/Od` etc. Fine.
   - It doesn't set `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY`; default is okay.
   - It sets flags even for non-Coverage configs; harmless.
   - It doesn't define `NDEBUG`? It does.
   - `/Zi` and `/DEBUG` both set; good.
   - `/Ob1` after `/O2`; good order.
   - Missing `/FS`? For parallel builds, `/FS` forces synchronous PDB writes; CMake may add `/FS`? With `/Zi` and shared PDB, parallel cl could conflict. Their earlier Makefile had `/FS` vs `/Fd` discussion. With CMake, CMake might not add `/FS`. If build/coverage uses `-j`, potential `C1041`. But Ninja default parallel. Their current Debug builds with `/Zi` and `-j` apparently work (they ran `ctest`, not necessarily parallel build). This is a risk to check. However, adding `/FS` or `/Fd` is a separate decision. Mention briefly.

6. **`message(FATAL_ERROR "..." "...")`** — multiple arguments concatenated without separator. Also "wasnt" apostrophe. Suggest one string with `\n` or space.

If user passes `coverage`, it won't match; `CMAKE_C_FLAGS_COVERAGE` variable is uppercase config name? CMake looks up `CMAKE_C_FLAGS_<CONFIG>` with the exact config string; `coverage` would look for `CMAKE_C_FLAGS_coverage`, not set. So document exact case. Could use `string(TOUPPER ...)` but not necessary.

```
execute_process(COMMAND "${MICROSOFT_COVERAGE}" --version OUTPUT_VARIABLE ... RESULT_VARIABLE ...)
to_major_minor(_cov_ver ...)
check_component(CodeCoverage "${_cov_ver}" "${TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_TESTED}" "${TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_MIN}")
```
And constants. Also `--version` output is `18.7.0-preview...`; regex `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` → 18.7. Good.

# Visual Studio 2026 release notes | Microsoft Learn

We're excited to announce the availability of the Visual Studio 2026 October update. This release marks the beginning of a new era for Visual Studio with deep platform integration of AI, stronger fundamentals, and improved performance.

Download [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) to enjoy these new features and improvements.

## Version 18.11.1

Released on **October 20, 2026**.

| Top bug fixes | From the community |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed issue debugging compose projects due to overeager failover to wslc | [Feedback ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Visual-Studio-CtrlF5-blocks-Docker-Comp/11160129) |
| Updating the installer to include the latest servicing release of the 10.0.26100 Windows SDK (10.0.26100.9457) |  |
| C++23 feature complete in IntelliSense minus modules support |  |

## October Update 18.11.0

Released on **October 13, 2026**.

### IDE

**Numbered document tab shortcuts ^📣^**

> 
> *Quickly jump to document tabs using industry-standard keyboard shortcuts.*
> 
> You can now quickly switch to open documents using Ctrl+Numpad1 through Ctrl+Numpad9. Each shortcut activates the corresponding visible document tab in the active document group, making it faster to navigate between files without reaching for the mouse.
> 
> ![Numbered tabs](media/18.11/numbered-tabs.png)
> 
> The numbering follows the document well's visual order, including both pinned and unpinned tabs. Preview tabs do not consume a shortcut slot, ensuring the numbering remains predictable. The shortcuts are scoped to the active document group, so switching groups updates the tab mapping automatically.
> 
> This behavior aligns Visual Studio with common editor conventions, making it easier to transition between development environments while maintaining a consistent keyboard-first workflow. The commands are available through keyboard customization and the command system.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Numbered-Tab-Shortcuts-in-Document-Well/477176) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Open Folder respects restore settings ^📣^**

> 
> *Open Folder now honors workspace restoration preferences.*
> 
> Visual Studio has long restored open documents and Solution Explorer state when reopening a folder. Previously, the *Reopen documents on solution load* and *Restore Solution Explorer project hierarchy state on solution load* settings only affected solution-based workflows, and Open Folder would restore the workspace regardless of those settings.
> 
> With this update, Open Folder now respects the same settings. If you disable either option, Visual Studio will no longer restore open documents or Solution Explorer state when reopening a folder.
> 
> To change these preferences, go to **Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → General** and configure *Reopen documents on solution load* and *Restore Solution Explorer project hierarchy state on solution load*. The selected behavior now applies consistently to both solutions and folders.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Reopen-documents-and-Restore-SolExp-h/10999326) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Never lose unsaved work - Hot Exit ^📣^**

> 
> *Hot Exit preserves unsaved files & saved files with unsaved changes, so you can pick up exactly where you left off.*
> 
> When enabled, Hot Exit saves your session state when you close Visual Studio. The next time you open Visual Studio, it restores your open documents, edits, and unsaved changes automatically, so you don't need to save manually.
> 
> To enable Hot Exit, go to **Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → General** and select **Reopen unsaved documents on solution load or empty environment**.
> 
> ![Projects and Solutions > General settings with Reopen unsaved documents on solution load or empty environment selected](media/18.11/hot-exit-settings.png)
> 
> Hot Exit preserves:
> 
> - Unsaved files.
> - Saved files with unsaved changes.
> - Undo functionality for saved files, including Ctrl+Z.
> - Your tab and window layout.
> 
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-ability-for-Visual-Studio-to-automat/10989739) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Fonts and Colors ^📣^**

> 
> *Customize Visual Studio with a modernized Fonts and Colors experience built on Unified Settings.*
> 
> Personalize Visual Studio with a modernized Fonts and Colors experience built on Unified Settings. Previously available through the legacy Tools > Options dialog, Fonts and Colors now benefits from the same settings platform used throughout Visual Studio.
> 
> ![Fonts & Colors settings page](media/18.11/fontsandcolor.png)
> 
> The new experience introduces category-based navigation, integrated search, inline previews, and an updated color editing experience. Foreground colors, background colors, font styles, and previews are displayed directly within the settings grid, making it easier to review existing customizations and update multiple settings without repeatedly selecting individual items.
> 
> ##### Backed by settings.json
> 
> Fonts and Colors settings now participate in Visual Studio's settings.json model. Changes made through the UI are reflected in settings.json, allowing advanced users to inspect, edit, share, or revert customizations directly through the file while keeping both experiences synchronized.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-a-search-box-in-Environment-Fonts/458349) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

### Productivity

**Hover tooltip delay setting ^📣^**

> 
> *Control how long you need to hover over code before the Quick Info tooltip appears, so it doesn't get in your way when you're moving the mouse around the editor.*
> 
> Hover tooltips in the editor have always appeared after a fixed 150 ms of hovering. If you move the mouse slowly, or just pass over code on your way somewhere else, that tooltip pops up over the exact line you were trying to click.
> 
> ![Quick Info delay](media/18.11/quickinfo.png)
> 
> You can now set that delay yourself.
> 
> **Tools → Options → Text Editor → Advanced → Quick Info hover delay (ms)**
> 
> The default is 150 ms, which is the value Visual Studio has always used, so nothing changes until you change it. Valid values are 50 to 10000 ms. Turn it up if tooltips get in your way, turn it down if you want them faster.
> 
> The setting applies immediately. No restart, no reopening files.
> 
> One note on scope: this controls the delay for hover handlers that don't request a specific timing of their own, which is what Quick Info uses. Extensions that ask for an explicit hover delay keep their own behavior.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Hover-Delay-Setting/780597) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Stop build on first failure ^📣^**

> 
> *You can now make Visual Studio stop the build after the first failure, instead of continuing to build the remaining projects.*
> 
> Visual Studio now includes an opt-in setting that stops a solution build after the first project failure. You can get back to fixing the error sooner instead of waiting for projects that can no longer produce a successful build.
> 
> Enable **Stop solution build after first failure** in **Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → Build and Run**. When you enable it, Visual Studio stops starting queued projects and safely stops projects already building. The build still reports as failed, not canceled. If you leave the setting disabled, build behavior stays the same.
> 
> ![Build time comparison chart with fail-fast enabled and disabled](media/18.11/fail-fast-chart.png)
> 
> This improvement can be substantial for large solutions. In testing, four regular builds averaged 26 seconds with the setting disabled and 1.5 seconds with it enabled - a **94% reduction** in post-failure completion time. Results vary by solution, but projects with longer dependency chains or many parallel builds are likely to benefit the most.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-option-to-stop-projects-building-if/355793) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Move documents with the keyboard ^📣^**

> 
> *Rearrange document tabs using a new keyboard shortcut that makes it easier to organize your workspace.*
> 
> You can now reorder the active tab in the document well without touching the mouse. Ctrl+Shift+PgUp moves the tab one visual position left, and Ctrl+Shift+PgDn moves it one position right. With vertical tabs enabled, the same shortcuts move the tab up and down instead, so the gesture stays the same whichever layout you prefer. The commands work for both documents and tool windows hosted in the document well.
> 
> Tab movement respects the structure you've already set up. Pinned and unpinned tabs keep their separation, so a tab won't jump across that boundary and quietly break your pinned set. In vertical tabs, a tab stays within its project group, and manual reordering is unavailable while alphabetical sorting is turned on. Preview tabs can't be moved.
> 
> Behind the shortcuts are two new global commands, **Window.MoveTabLeft** and **Window.MoveTabRight**, both listed in **Tools → Options → Environment → Keyboard** if you'd rather bind them somewhere else. The defaults take over the previous Text Editor bindings for **Edit.ViewTopExtend** and **Edit.ViewBottomExtend**; those commands are still available and can be reassigned to any shortcut you like.
> 
> Thanks to everyone who voted for this on Developer Community. Ctrl+Shift+PgUp/PgDn is the same binding most browsers use, so it should feel familiar from the first press.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Keyboard-shortcut-for-moving-tabs/1337230) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Reset zoom keyboard shortcut ^📣^**

> 
> *If you've zoomed in or out of the editor, you can now reset the zoom level to 100% with a new keyboard shortcut.*
> 
> Press Ctrl+NumPad0 to snap the editor zoom level straight back to 100%. Zoom in to inspect a dense block of code, zoom out to get a sense of a file's shape, then return to your normal view with a single keystroke.
> 
> Until now, getting back to 100% meant nudging the zoom with Ctrl+MouseWheel until it looked about right, or picking the value from the zoom control in the corner of the editor. That's easy to overshoot, and it's especially annoying when a sensitive mouse wheel changes the zoom without you asking. The new shortcut removes the guesswork and keeps a consistent editing view as you move between files.
> 
> The shortcut is backed by a new View.ZoomReset command. Ctrl+NumPad0 matches the binding used in VS Code and most browsers, but if you'd rather use something else, or you're on a keyboard without a number pad, you can remap it in **Tools → Options → Environment → Keyboard**.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Reset-zoom-via-keyboard-shortcut/1373025) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**New markdown template ^📣^**

> 
> *You can now create a new markdown file from the New File dialog.*
> 
> You can now create a Markdown file directly from the **New File** dialog. Press Ctrl+N, select Markdown, and start writing without manually creating a file or setting its extension.
> 
> ![Markdown template](media/18.11/markdown-template.png)
> 
> This workflow makes it faster to create notes, documentation, and other Markdown content. It also works with Hot Exit, which restores your unsaved files when you restart Visual Studio so you can continue where you left off.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Cannot-create-a-Markdown-file-by-New-Fi/10966564) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

### GitHub Copilot

**Try the new Copilot chat experience**

> 
> *A refreshed Copilot chat, built on the Copilot SDK that powers Copilot everywhere.*
> 
> There's a new Copilot chat experience in Visual Studio, built on the Copilot SDK, the same foundation that powers the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app. It's the next step in the journey that started with Agent (Preview), the first Visual Studio experience built on the SDK. Now that same foundation powers the whole chat experience, including Ask mode, Agent mode, and the underlying chat infrastructure.
> 
> Building on a shared foundation means Visual Studio gets better as Copilot gets better. When you turn it on, you get:
> 
> - **More capable agent workflows** that handle end-to-end tasks with less back-and-forth.
> - **Longer-running sessions** with more effective prompt caching for better performance.
> - **Consistent behavior** across every Copilot surface.
> 
> 
> ##### Turn it on
> 
> 1. In Visual Studio, go to **Tools → Options**.
> 2. Go to **GitHub → Copilot → Copilot Chat**.
> 3. Check **Use new Copilot chat experience**.
> 4. Restart Visual Studio for the change to take effect.
> 
> 
> ![The new Copilot Chat experience in Visual Studio](media/18.11/new-chat-experience.png)
> 
> Then use it on the work you already do: feature changes, bug fixes, refactors, and everything in between.
> 
> We'd love your feedback. If something is missing or not working, send it through **Help → Send Feedback → Report a Problem** so we know what to prioritize next. 

### Git tooling

**Compare a commit to your working tree ^📣^**

> 
> *See what's changed between a commit and your code today.*
> 
> You can now compare any commit directly to your working tree, so you can see exactly what's changed since that point.
> 
> From commit history or the branch list, right-click a commit and select **Compare with Working Tree**. It opens a compare view where you can click through the diffs against your working tree without checking out the commit.
> 
> ![Context menu on a commit in the History graph showing the Compare with Working Tree command](media/18.11/compare-commit-working-tree-command.png)
> 
> ![Side-by-side diff comparing a commit to the working tree, with the list of changed files on the right](media/18.11/compare-commit-working-tree-view.png)
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/content/idea/370956/allow-compare-working-copy-to-historical-version-v.html) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Bulk resolve merge conflicts ^📣^**

> 
> *Skip resolving conflicts one file at a time: keep or take them all at once.*
> 
> Resolving conflicts one file at a time gets old fast when a merge touches dozens of them.
>

> 
> ![Context menu on a folder under Unmerged Changes in Git Changes, showing Keep All Current and Take All Incoming options](media/18.11/bulk-resolve-conflicts-menu.png)
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/When-resolving-merge-conflicts-allow-us/1470684) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

## September Update 18.10.0

Released on **September 8, 2026**.

### GitHub Copilot

**Updates to Bring Your Own Key ^📣^**

> 
> *Use AI in Visual Studio with the models your team prefers - through GitHub Copilot or your own model deployments, signed in to GitHub or not.*
> 
> The best AI in Visual Studio is the AI you can bring with you. With Bring Your Own Key (BYOK), more developers can use AI in Visual Studio with the models their teams prefer - whether through GitHub Copilot or their own model deployments. From individual developers experimenting with new models to organizations standardizing on approved deployments, BYOK lets you use AI your way, whether or not you're signed in to GitHub.
> 
> BYOK is available in preview and enabled by default across the Community, Professional, and Enterprise SKUs. Connect to a Microsoft Foundry deployment or use a key from another supported provider, then work in Agent Mode with the new Agent (Preview).
> 
> This is an early preview, and we want your feedback. Not every model supports every Agent Mode capability yet. When a feature isn't supported, Visual Studio marks it clearly instead of failing silently. Try it and tell us what's working and where we should invest next in the [Developer Community forum](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/VisualStudio/suggest) or [fill out this short survey](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/dkVUtjRJ3Y).
> 
> To get started:
> 
> 1. Open **Chat**.
> 2. Open the model picker and choose **Add a model** or **Manage Models**.
> 3. Connect to your provider.
> 4. Start working in Agent Mode.
> 
> 
> Supported providers: Microsoft Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama and custom endpoint support for OpenAI and Ollama.
> 
> 
> > 
> > **This release has breaking changes for the BYOK capability:**
> > 
> > - BYOK now works with the new Agent (Preview), which is built on the GitHub Copilot SDK-powered harness. The earlier BYOK experience in the previous Ask and Agent modes is no longer supported. Install the latest Visual Studio Insiders release (18.10) and use the new Agent (Preview) to try it.
> > - Previously added Ollama models within 18.10 Insiders 1 will need to be re-added in 18.10 Insiders 2 due to a few backend updates for that provider.
> > 
> 
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Custom-URLs-for-Models-in-Copilot-Chat/10956896?q=bring+your+own+model+copilot&sort=votes&stateGroup=active&ftype=idea) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Explore PRs with the Git agent**

> 
> *Explore pull requests in chat and navigate directly to comments and files.*
> 
> Reviewing a pull request often means piecing together the discussion, the changed files, and what actually matters before you can dig in. The **Git agent** can now do that legwork for you.
> 
> Open **Copilot Chat**, select the **Git agent**, and ask it about your pull request, attaching the PR as context from the **Git Repository** window.
> 
> The response includes navigable links that open the corresponding comments and files directly in the pull request view in the IDE. Ask follow-up questions any time you want the agent to go deeper.
> 
> ![Navigable links in the Git agent response opening a file in the pull request view](media/18.10/pr-exploration.png)
> 
> Connect your Git provider's MCP servers so Copilot can get more context about your PRs. GitHub and Azure DevOps are both supported. 

### Debugging & diagnostics

**See Which Operand Decides Your if Condition**

> 
> *Quickly see which expression determines your if condition with inline branch highlighting.*
> 
> Want to quickly understand why a compound condition took a particular branch? Visual Studio now highlights the deciding expression in C# `if` statements that use `&&` or `||`.
> 
> While debugging, pause on an `if` statement. Alongside the existing inline `→ true` or `→ false` hint, Visual Studio uses red and green highlighting to show which operand determined the result.
> 
> For example, when an `&&` condition evaluates to false, the highlighting identifies the operand that failed or caused evaluation to short-circuit. When an `||` condition evaluates to true, it identifies the operand that satisfied the condition. This helps you understand complex branching behavior without evaluating each expression individually.
> 
> ![Inline highlighting showing the operand that satisfied a true condition](media/18.10/highlighting-true.png)
> 
> ![Inline highlighting showing the operand that caused a false condition](media/18.10/highlighting-false.png)
> 
> You can right-click a highlighted expression to disable branch highlighting from the editor context menu. The highlight formats are also available under **Tools → Options → Environment → Fonts and Colors**. You can customize them using colors that work best with your preferred Visual Studio theme. 

**Attach to Process now supports Podman containers**

> 
> *Attach the Visual Studio debugger to processes inside Podman containers, just like Docker.*
> 
> Starting in Visual Studio 18.10, container discovery recognizes Podman alongside Docker.
> 
> Start a container, then go to **Debug → Attach to Process**. Set **Connection type** to **Podman**, then click **Find**. Your Podman containers appear automatically, with the same attach experience you already use for Docker.
> 
> You can debug both .NET and C++ containers with no extra configuration.
> 
> ![Attach to Process dialog showing Podman containers discovered](media/18.10/podman-support.gif)

## August Update 18.9.0

Released on **August 11, 2026**

### GitHub Copilot

**Adjust model thinking effort to match your task**

> 
> *Choose low, medium, or high thinking effort for supported models to balance response quality and token usage.*
> 
> You can now control how much a model reasons through a problem. Visual Studio 18.9 adds thinking effort controls for supported models, so you can choose low, medium, or high effort based on your task and token budget.
> 
> ##### How thinking effort works
> 
> Some Copilot models now support adjustable thinking levels:
> 
> - **Low** - Gives quick responses with minimal reasoning. Best for straightforward questions and code suggestions. Uses fewer tokens.
> - **Medium** - Balances reasoning depth and response speed. Best for everyday coding tasks.
> - **High** - Uses deeper reasoning for complex problems. Best for tricky algorithms, architecture decisions, and hard-to-debug issues. Uses more tokens.
> 
> 
> You can adjust thinking effort from the **Model picker** or the expanded **Model management** view. Lower levels help you stay within your token budget while still getting useful support for each task.
> 
> ![Model management view showing a thinking effort dropdown with low, medium, and high options](media/18.9/manage-models-view.png)

**Review changes and commits with the Git agent**

> 
> *Catch issues before the pull request.*
> 
> You don't have to wait for a pull request to get a second set of eyes on your code. Ask the **Git agent** to review your changes or commits as you work.
>

> 
> Switch to the **Git agent** in Copilot Chat and ask it to review your changes. The agent looks at your uncommitted work and surfaces comments inline in the editor. The **Git Changes** view gives you a navigable list so you can jump to each comment quickly.

> You can also kick off a commit review directly from the **Git Changes** infobar after committing, or from any commit in the **Git Repository** window.

> From the Submodules section, you can add, update, and remove submodules. Visual Studio also discovers and activates submodules automatically when you open a solution or folder, and keeps them out of the general local repositories list to reduce clutter.
> 
> ![Repository picker showing parent and submodule hierarchy](media/18.9/git-submodule-support-select-repo.png)
> 
> Submodules are read-only by default. If you want to work inside a submodule instead of only consuming it, go to **Tools → Options → Source Control → Git**, find **Automatically activate multiple repositories**, and select **Yes, include submodules**.
> 
> This is the first milestone in an evolving experience, and more improvements are planned for future releases.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/full-git-submodule-support/351549) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Worktrees: work on multiple branches at once ^📣^**

> 
> *Create, open, and manage Git worktrees to work on multiple branches simultaneously without stashing or re-cloning.*
> 
> If you've ever stashed half-finished work just to check another branch, worktrees let you skip that step. Each worktree is a separate working directory for the same repo, so your in-progress work stays untouched while you work elsewhere.
> 
> In the **Git Repository** window, right-click any branch and select **New Worktree from** to create a worktree. You can start from a new branch or use the selected branch. You can also create a worktree from any commit in the history graph. Open it in your current window or in a new Visual Studio instance to work on both branches side by side.
> 
> ![Context menu on a branch showing New Worktree From, Open Worktree in Current Window, Open Worktree in New Window, and Delete Worktree options](media/18.9/git-worktrees-context-menu.png)
> 
> Worktrees appear inline with your branches. You can switch between them from the branch list, branch picker, or repo picker. When you're done, right-click the worktree and select **Delete Worktree** to clean up.
> 
> ![Git Repository branch list with worktrees shown alongside branches](media/18.9/git-worktrees-branch-list.png)
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Git-worktree-support-in-the-Visual-Studi/10708556) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Review commits with Copilot**

> 
> *Get a private Copilot code review on your commits.*
> 
> Copilot code review already gives you feedback on uncommitted changes. Now you can run the same review on committed changes.
> 
> Right-click any commit in the **Git Repository** window and select **Review Commit** to review that commit. Select two commits to review everything that changed between them.
> 
> ![Right-click context menu showing Review Commit option in Git Repository window](media/18.9/copilot-commit-review-context-menu.png)
> 
> You can also reference a commit in Copilot Chat and ask the **Git agent** to review it.
> 
> ![Copilot Chat window with Git agent prompt asking to review a specific commit](media/18.9/copilot-commit-review-git-agent.png)
> 
> Copilot's review comments appear inline in the changed files. A single commit opens in the **Commit Details** window. A two-commit range opens in the **Compare Commits** view. Select any comment to jump directly to that code.
> 
> ![Inline Copilot review comment displayed in the Commit Details window](media/18.9/copilot-commit-review-comments.png)
> 
> Reviews stay local to your Visual Studio session and work with both GitHub and Azure DevOps repositories.
> 
> To enable this feature, go to **Tools → Options → GitHub → Copilot → Source Control Integration** and turn on **Review Git changes locally and provide suggestions from comments**. 

**Compare a file to your working tree ^📣^**

> 
> *Compare an earlier version of a file with your current local changes.*
> 
> Want to see how a file changed since an earlier commit? You can now compare any file version with your current working tree.
> 
> In **Solution Explorer**, right-click the file and select **Git → View History**. Then, in the file history, right-click a commit and select **Compare with Working Tree**.
> 
> ![Context menu in file history showing Compare with Working Tree](media/18.9/compare-working-tree-history-menu.png)
> 
> Visual Studio opens a diff with the commit version on the left and your working tree version on the right. You can review all changes since that commit, including committed and uncommitted edits.
> 
> ![Diff view showing committed file version on left and working tree version on right](media/18.9/compare-working-tree-diff.png)
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/content/idea/370956/allow-compare-working-copy-to-historical-version-v.html) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**PR review updates - autocomplete and timeline ^📣^**

> 
> *Set a pull request to complete automatically and see its update history in Visual Studio.*
>

# Visual Studio 2026 release notes | Microsoft Learn

We're excited to announce the availability of the Visual Studio 2026 October update. This release marks the beginning of a new era for Visual Studio with deep platform integration of AI, stronger fundamentals, and improved performance.

Download [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) to enjoy these new features and improvements.

## Version 18.11.1

Released on **October 20, 2026**.

| Top bug fixes | From the community |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed issue debugging compose projects due to overeager failover to wslc | [Feedback ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Visual-Studio-CtrlF5-blocks-Docker-Comp/11160129) |
| Updating the installer to include the latest servicing release of the 10.0.26100 Windows SDK (10.0.26100.9457) |  |
| C++23 feature complete in IntelliSense minus modules support |  |

## October Update 18.11.0

Released on **October 13, 2026**.

### IDE

**Numbered document tab shortcuts ^📣^**

> 
> *Quickly jump to document tabs using industry-standard keyboard shortcuts.*
> 
> You can now quickly switch to open documents using Ctrl+Numpad1 through Ctrl+Numpad9. Each shortcut activates the corresponding visible document tab in the active document group, making it faster to navigate between files without reaching for the mouse.
> 
> ![Numbered tabs](media/18.11/numbered-tabs.png)
> 
> The numbering follows the document well's visual order, including both pinned and unpinned tabs. Preview tabs do not consume a shortcut slot, ensuring the numbering remains predictable. The shortcuts are scoped to the active document group, so switching groups updates the tab mapping automatically.
> 
> This behavior aligns Visual Studio with common editor conventions, making it easier to transition between development environments while maintaining a consistent keyboard-first workflow. The commands are available through keyboard customization and the command system.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Numbered-Tab-Shortcuts-in-Document-Well/477176) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Open Folder respects restore settings ^📣^**

> 
> *Open Folder now honors workspace restoration preferences.*
> 
> Visual Studio has long restored open documents and Solution Explorer state when reopening a folder. Previously, the *Reopen documents on solution load* and *Restore Solution Explorer project hierarchy state on solution load* settings only affected solution-based workflows, and Open Folder would restore the workspace regardless of those settings.
> 
> With this update, Open Folder now respects the same settings. If you disable either option, Visual Studio will no longer restore open documents or Solution Explorer state when reopening a folder.
> 
> To change these preferences, go to **Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → General** and configure *Reopen documents on solution load* and *Restore Solution Explorer project hierarchy state on solution load*. The selected behavior now applies consistently to both solutions and folders.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Reopen-documents-and-Restore-SolExp-h/10999326) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Never lose unsaved work - Hot Exit ^📣^**

> 
> *Hot Exit preserves unsaved files & saved files with unsaved changes, so you can pick up exactly where you left off.*
> 
> When enabled, Hot Exit saves your session state when you close Visual Studio. The next time you open Visual Studio, it restores your open documents, edits, and unsaved changes automatically, so you don't need to save manually.
> 
> To enable Hot Exit, go to **Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → General** and select **Reopen unsaved documents on solution load or empty environment**.
> 
> ![Projects and Solutions > General settings with Reopen unsaved documents on solution load or empty environment selected](media/18.11/hot-exit-settings.png)
> 
> Hot Exit preserves:
> 
> - Unsaved files.
> - Saved files with unsaved changes.
> - Undo functionality for saved files, including Ctrl+Z.
> - Your tab and window layout.
> 
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-ability-for-Visual-Studio-to-automat/10989739) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Fonts and Colors ^📣^**

> 
> *Customize Visual Studio with a modernized Fonts and Colors experience built on Unified Settings.*
> 
> Personalize Visual Studio with a modernized Fonts and Colors experience built on Unified Settings. Previously available through the legacy Tools > Options dialog, Fonts and Colors now benefits from the same settings platform used throughout Visual Studio.
> 
> ![Fonts & Colors settings page](media/18.11/fontsandcolor.png)
> 
> The new experience introduces category-based navigation, integrated search, inline previews, and an updated color editing experience. Foreground colors, background colors, font styles, and previews are displayed directly within the settings grid, making it easier to review existing customizations and update multiple settings without repeatedly selecting individual items.
> 
> ##### Backed by settings.json
> 
> Fonts and Colors settings now participate in Visual Studio's settings.json model. Changes made through the UI are reflected in settings.json, allowing advanced users to inspect, edit, share, or revert customizations directly through the file while keeping both experiences synchronized.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-a-search-box-in-Environment-Fonts/458349) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

### Productivity

**Hover tooltip delay setting ^📣^**

> 
> *Control how long you need to hover over code before the Quick Info tooltip appears, so it doesn't get in your way when you're moving the mouse around the editor.*
> 
> Hover tooltips in the editor have always appeared after a fixed 150 ms of hovering. If you move the mouse slowly, or just pass over code on your way somewhere else, that tooltip pops up over the exact line you were trying to click.
> 
> ![Quick Info delay](media/18.11/quickinfo.png)
> 
> You can now set that delay yourself.
> 
> **Tools → Options → Text Editor → Advanced → Quick Info hover delay (ms)**
> 
> The default is 150 ms, which is the value Visual Studio has always used, so nothing changes until you change it. Valid values are 50 to 10000 ms. Turn it up if tooltips get in your way, turn it down if you want them faster.
> 
> The setting applies immediately. No restart, no reopening files.
> 
> One note on scope: this controls the delay for hover handlers that don't request a specific timing of their own, which is what Quick Info uses. Extensions that ask for an explicit hover delay keep their own behavior.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Hover-Delay-Setting/780597) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Stop build on first failure ^📣^**

> 
> *You can now make Visual Studio stop the build after the first failure, instead of continuing to build the remaining projects.*
> 
> Visual Studio now includes an opt-in setting that stops a solution build after the first project failure. You can get back to fixing the error sooner instead of waiting for projects that can no longer produce a successful build.
> 
> Enable **Stop solution build after first failure** in **Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → Build and Run**. When you enable it, Visual Studio stops starting queued projects and safely stops projects already building. The build still reports as failed, not canceled. If you leave the setting disabled, build behavior stays the same.
> 
> ![Build time comparison chart with fail-fast enabled and disabled](media/18.11/fail-fast-chart.png)
> 
> This improvement can be substantial for large solutions. In testing, four regular builds averaged 26 seconds with the setting disabled and 1.5 seconds with it enabled - a **94% reduction** in post-failure completion time. Results vary by solution, but projects with longer dependency chains or many parallel builds are likely to benefit the most.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-option-to-stop-projects-building-if/355793) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Move documents with the keyboard ^📣^**

> 
> *Rearrange document tabs using a new keyboard shortcut that makes it easier to organize your workspace.*
> 
> You can now reorder the active tab in the document well without touching the mouse. Ctrl+Shift+PgUp moves the tab one visual position left, and Ctrl+Shift+PgDn moves it one position right. With vertical tabs enabled, the same shortcuts move the tab up and down instead, so the gesture stays the same whichever layout you prefer. The commands work for both documents and tool windows hosted in the document well.
> 
> Tab movement respects the structure you've already set up. Pinned and unpinned tabs keep their separation, so a tab won't jump across that boundary and quietly break your pinned set. In vertical tabs, a tab stays within its project group, and manual reordering is unavailable while alphabetical sorting is turned on. Preview tabs can't be moved.
> 
> Behind the shortcuts are two new global commands, **Window.MoveTabLeft** and **Window.MoveTabRight**, both listed in **Tools → Options → Environment → Keyboard** if you'd rather bind them somewhere else. The defaults take over the previous Text Editor bindings for **Edit.ViewTopExtend** and **Edit.ViewBottomExtend**; those commands are still available and can be reassigned to any shortcut you like.
> 
> Thanks to everyone who voted for this on Developer Community. Ctrl+Shift+PgUp/PgDn is the same binding most browsers use, so it should feel familiar from the first press.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Keyboard-shortcut-for-moving-tabs/1337230) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Reset zoom keyboard shortcut ^📣^**

> 
> *If you've zoomed in or out of the editor, you can now reset the zoom level to 100% with a new keyboard shortcut.*
> 
> Press Ctrl+NumPad0 to snap the editor zoom level straight back to 100%. Zoom in to inspect a dense block of code, zoom out to get a sense of a file's shape, then return to your normal view with a single keystroke.
> 
> Until now, getting back to 100% meant nudging the zoom with Ctrl+MouseWheel until it looked about right, or picking the value from the zoom control in the corner of the editor. That's easy to overshoot, and it's especially annoying when a sensitive mouse wheel changes the zoom without you asking. The new shortcut removes the guesswork and keeps a consistent editing view as you move between files.
> 
> The shortcut is backed by a new View.ZoomReset command. Ctrl+NumPad0 matches the binding used in VS Code and most browsers, but if you'd rather use something else, or you're on a keyboard without a number pad, you can remap it in **Tools → Options → Environment → Keyboard**.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Reset-zoom-via-keyboard-shortcut/1373025) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**New markdown template ^📣^**

> 
> *You can now create a new markdown file from the New File dialog.*
> 
> You can now create a Markdown file directly from the **New File** dialog. Press Ctrl+N, select Markdown, and start writing without manually creating a file or setting its extension.
> 
> ![Markdown template](media/18.11/markdown-template.png)
> 
> This workflow makes it faster to create notes, documentation, and other Markdown content. It also works with Hot Exit, which restores your unsaved files when you restart Visual Studio so you can continue where you left off.
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Cannot-create-a-Markdown-file-by-New-Fi/10966564) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

### GitHub Copilot

**Try the new Copilot chat experience**

> 
> *A refreshed Copilot chat, built on the Copilot SDK that powers Copilot everywhere.*
> 
> There's a new Copilot chat experience in Visual Studio, built on the Copilot SDK, the same foundation that powers the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app. It's the next step in the journey that started with Agent (Preview), the first Visual Studio experience built on the SDK. Now that same foundation powers the whole chat experience, including Ask mode, Agent mode, and the underlying chat infrastructure.
> 
> Building on a shared foundation means Visual Studio gets better as Copilot gets better. When you turn it on, you get:
> 
> - **More capable agent workflows** that handle end-to-end tasks with less back-and-forth.
> - **Longer-running sessions** with more effective prompt caching for better performance.
> - **Consistent behavior** across every Copilot surface.
> 
> 
> ##### Turn it on
> 
> 1. In Visual Studio, go to **Tools → Options**.
> 2. Go to **GitHub → Copilot → Copilot Chat**.
> 3. Check **Use new Copilot chat experience**.
> 4. Restart Visual Studio for the change to take effect.
> 
> 
> ![The new Copilot Chat experience in Visual Studio](media/18.11/new-chat-experience.png)
> 
> Then use it on the work you already do: feature changes, bug fixes, refactors, and everything in between.
> 
> We'd love your feedback. If something is missing or not working, send it through **Help → Send Feedback → Report a Problem** so we know what to prioritize next. 

### Git tooling

**Compare a commit to your working tree ^📣^**

> 
> *See what's changed between a commit and your code today.*
> 
> You can now compare any commit directly to your working tree, so you can see exactly what's changed since that point.
> 
> From commit history or the branch list, right-click a commit and select **Compare with Working Tree**. It opens a compare view where you can click through the diffs against your working tree without checking out the commit.
> 
> ![Context menu on a commit in the History graph showing the Compare with Working Tree command](media/18.11/compare-commit-working-tree-command.png)
> 
> ![Side-by-side diff comparing a commit to the working tree, with the list of changed files on the right](media/18.11/compare-commit-working-tree-view.png)
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/content/idea/370956/allow-compare-working-copy-to-historical-version-v.html) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

**Bulk resolve merge conflicts ^📣^**

> 
> *Skip resolving conflicts one file at a time: keep or take them all at once.*
> 
> Resolving conflicts one file at a time gets old fast when a merge touches dozens of them.
> 
> In **Git Changes**, right-click any file, folder, or the repo root under **Unmerged Changes** and select **Keep All Current** or **Take All Incoming** to resolve everything underneath it in one step.
> 
> ![Context menu on a folder under Unmerged Changes in Git Changes, showing Keep All Current and Take All Incoming options](media/18.11/bulk-resolve-conflicts-menu.png)
> 
> 📣 *See [feature ticket](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/When-resolving-merge-conflicts-allow-us/1470684) to share your feedback and continue the conversation.*

## September Update 18.10.0

Released on **September 8, 2026**.

### GitHub Copilot

**Updates to Bring Your Own Key ^📣^**

> 
> *Use AI in Visual Studio with the models your team prefers - through GitHub Copilot or your own model deployments, signed in to GitHub or not.*
> 
> The best AI in Visual Studio is the AI you can bring with you. With Bring Your Own Key (BYOK), more developers can use AI in Visual Studio with the models their teams prefer - whether through GitHub Copilot or their own model deployments. From individual developers experimenting with new models to organizations standardizing on approved deployments, BYOK lets you use AI your way, whether or not you're signed in to GitHub.
> 
> BYOK is available in preview and enabled by default across the Community, Professional, and Enterprise SKUs. Connect to a Microsoft Foundry deployment or use a key from another supported provider, then work in Agent Mode with the new Agent (Preview).
> 
> This is an early preview, and we want your feedback. Not every model supports every Agent Mode capability yet. When a feature isn't supported, Visual Studio marks it clearly instead of failing silently. Try it and tell us what's working and where we should invest next in the [Developer Community forum](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/VisualStudio/suggest) or [fill out this short survey](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/dkVUtjRJ3Y).
> 
> To get started:
> 
> 1. Open **Chat**.
> 2. Open the model picker and choose **Add a model** or **Manage Models**.
> 3. Connect to your provider.
> 4. Start working in Agent Mode.
> 
> 
> Supported providers: Microsoft Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama and custom endpoint support for OpenAI and Ollama.
> 
> 
> >

> > 
> > - BYOK now works with the new Agent (Preview), which is built on the GitHub Copilot SDK-powered harness. The earlier BYOK experience in the previous Ask and Agent modes is no longer supported. Install the latest Visual Studio Insiders release (18.10) and use the new Agent (Preview) to try it.
> > - Previously added Ollama models within 18.10 Insiders 1 will need to be re-added in 18.10 Insiders 2 due to a few backend updates for that provider.
> > 
> 
>

**Explore PRs with the Git agent**

> 
> *Explore pull requests in chat and navigate directly to comments and files.*
> 
> Reviewing a pull request often means piecing together the discussion, the changed files, and what actually matters before you can dig in. The **Git agent** can now do that legwork for you.
> 
> Open **Copilot Chat**, select the **Git agent**, and ask it about your pull request, attaching the PR as context from the **Git Repository** window.
> 
> The response includes navigable links that open the corresponding comments and files directly in the pull request view in the IDE. Ask follow-up questions any time you want the agent to go deeper.

### Debugging & diagnostics

**See Which Operand Decides Your if Condition**

> 
> *Quickly see which expression determines your if condition with inline branch highlighting.*
> 
> Want to quickly understand why a compound condition took a particular branch? Visual Studio now highlights the deciding expression in C# `if` statements that use `&&` or `||`.
> 
> While debugging, pause on an `if` statement. Alongside the existing inline `→ true` or `→ false` hint, Visual Studio uses red and green highlighting to show which operand determined the result.
> 
> For example, when an `&&` condition evaluates to false, the highlighting identifies the operand that failed or caused evaluation to short-circuit. When an `||` condition evaluates to true, it identifies the operand that satisfied the condition. This helps you understand complex branching behavior without evaluating each expression individually.
> 
> ![Inline highlighting showing the operand that satisfied a true condition](media/18.10/highlighting-true.png)
> 
> ![Inline highlighting showing the operand that caused a false condition](media/18.10/highlighting-false.png)
> 
> You can right-click a highlighted expression to disable branch highlighting from the editor context menu. The highlight formats are also available under **Tools → Options → Environment → Fonts and Colors**. You can customize them using colors that work best with your preferred Visual Studio theme. 

**Attach to Process now supports Podman containers**

> 
> *Attach the Visual Studio debugger to processes inside Podman containers, just like Docker.*
> 
> Starting in Visual Studio 18.10, container discovery recognizes Podman alongside Docker.
> 
> Start a container, then go to **Debug → Attach to Process**. Set **Connection type** to **Podman**, then click **Find**. Your Podman containers appear automatically, with the same attach experience you already use for Docker.
> 
> You can debug both .NET and C++ containers with no extra configuration.
> 
> ![Attach to Process dialog showing Podman containers discovered](media/18.10/podman-support.gif)

## August Update 18.9.0

Released on **August 11, 2026**

### GitHub Copilot

**Adjust model thinking effort to match your task**

> 
> *Choose low, medium, or high thinking effort for supported models to balance response quality and token usage.*
> 
> You can now control how much a model reasons through a problem. Visual Studio 18.9 adds thinking effort controls for supported models, so you can choose low, medium, or high effort based on your task and token budget.
> 
> ##### How thinking effort works
> 
> Some Copilot models now support adjustable thinking levels:
> 
> - **Low** - Gives quick responses with minimal reasoning. Best for straightforward questions and code suggestions. Uses fewer tokens.
> - **Medium** - Balances reasoning depth and response speed. Best for everyday coding tasks.
> - **High** - Uses deeper reasoning for complex problems. Best for tricky algorithms, architecture decisions, and hard-to-debug issues. Uses more tokens.
> 
> 
> You can adjust thinking effort from the **Model picker** or the expanded **Model management** view. Lower levels help you stay within your token budget while still getting useful support for each task.
> 
> ![Model management view showing a thinking effort dropdown with low, medium, and high options](media/18.9/manage-models-view.png)

**Review changes and commits with the Git agent**

> 
> *Catch issues before the pull request.*
> 
> You don't have to wait for a pull request to get a second set of eyes on your code. Ask the **Git agent** to review your changes or commits as you work.
> 
> ##### Review uncommitted changes
> 
> Switch to the **Git agent** in Copilot Chat and ask it to review your changes. The agent looks at your uncommitted work and surfaces comments inline in the editor. The **Git Changes** view gives you a navigable list so you can jump to each comment quickly.
> 
> You can also select the Copilot review icon in the **Git Changes** window to start a review.
> 
> ![Inline review comments in the editor and a per-file comment list in the Copilot Chat panel](media/18.9/git-agent-changes-review-comment-2.png)
> 
> ##### Review a commit
> 
> Attach a commit as context in Copilot Chat and ask the **Git agent** to review it. Review comments appear inline on the changed files in a commit-specific view, separate from your working files.
> 
> You can also kick off a commit review directly from the **Git Changes** infobar after committing, or from any commit in the **Git Repository** window.
> 
> ![Inline review comments on a commit, with per-file findings in the Copilot Chat panel](media/18.9/git-agent-commit-review-comment-1.png)
> 
> When you start a review through Copilot Chat, keep the conversation going to dig into findings, get explanations, or work on suggested fixes. Reviews work with both GitHub and Azure DevOps repositories and use the [GitHub Copilot code review service](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/request-a-code-review/use-code-review?tool=visualstudio). 

**Organization-level custom agents**

> 
> *GitHub organization owners can now add custom agents across their organization.*

> 
> When you work in repositories in your organization, Visual Studio automatically detects org-level custom agents and shows them in the agent picker. Hover over an agent to see its description and organization source. Click the definition button to open the agent definition file.
> 
> ![Agent picker dropdown showing organization-level custom agents, descriptions, and definition buttons](media/18.9/org-level-agent.png)
> 
> Set up org-level custom agents to support your team's workflow.

1. Is docs-based minimum "bad" because untested? Or normal?
- Normal and standard. A minimum supported version is a policy/contract, usually based on documented feature/API availability, not exhaustive testing. Projects test a representative matrix; it's impractical to test every version. What matters:
  - the min is justified by a specific requirement (feature, ABI, compiler support);
  - it's labeled "minimum supported" vs "tested";

- Risk: if docs are wrong or feature has bugs in that version, users on min may fail. Mitigation: test min in CI/VM when feasible; otherwise mark as untested. For a student project, acceptable.
- "Плохо" only if you claim "tested on min" without testing, or if the min is arbitrary (e.g., current version minus random). Docs-based is defensible.

  Line 33: - **Ускорение сборки больших проектов.** Прекомпилированные заголовки (PCH, Precompiled Headers): `/Yc` и `/Yu` в MSVC, `-include` в GCC/Clang, `target_precompile_headers` в CMake. Что попадает в PCH (тяжёлые редко меняющиеся заголовки — STL, Qt, `Windows.h`, boost) и что нет (свои часто меняющиеся заголовки). Почему PCH ломаются при изменении флагов компиляции и состава включений — и почему это полезный сигнал, а не баг. Смежные приёмы: unity-builds (склеивание нескольких `.cpp` в одну единицу трансляции — `CMAKE_UNITY_BUILD`), кеш компиляции `ccache` / `sccache`, распределённая сборка (`distcc`, `Incredibuild`). Trade-off: PCH ускоряет инкрементальную сборку в 2–10×, но скрывает забытые `#include` (TU собирается через PCH, а на чужой машине без PCH ломается). *Потенциал 0.3..0.5 баллов*

This is a crucial nuance: presence in Catalog.json ≠ included in Build Tools / selected workload.

The layout has `Microsoft.VisualStudio.BuildTools.Resources`, `Microsoft.VisualStudio.VC.DevCmd`, etc. It downloaded only MSBuildTools workload. No CodeCoverage payload. So the user's finding in Catalog.json only proves the package exists in the **VS 18.0.0 catalog**, not that it's part of Build Tools or installed by default.

However, `Catalog.json` may include all packages available to the channel; the package could be installable in Build Tools if selected. To prove Build Tools includes it, need to inspect the component graph: which package group/component references `Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.Targeted`, and whether that component is part of Build Tools product or a recommended/optional component. Also perhaps the `ChannelManifest.json` lists selected packages; and `Response.json` shows the layout selection.

Let's parse Catalog.json with PowerShell `ConvertFrom-Json` (read-only; 9.9 MB, fine). Look at `packages` array; find package IDs `Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console.Targeted`, `Microsoft.VisualStudio.PackageGroup.TestTools.CodeCoverage`, `Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.DynamicCodeCoverage`. Also search for dependencies referencing these IDs. And inspect `ChannelManifest.json` for selected packages/components; `Layout.json`/`Response.json` (small) for selection.

- `$j = Get-Content Catalog.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json; $j.packages | Where-Object { $_.id -match 'CodeCoverage' } | Select id, version, type, chip, productArch | Format-Table`

- Find references: `$j.packages | Where-Object { $_.dependencies -match 'CodeCoverage' } | Select id`.
- `Catalog.json` structure: `packages` array; each package has `id`, `version`, `type`, `dependencies` maybe object with `id`. Let's inspect one.
- `ChannelManifest.json` structure: `channelItems` with `id`, `version`, `type`, `payloads`; maybe lists selected packages. `Layout.json`/`Response.json` might show what was downloaded.

Let's do.

## Что за компоненты

| ID | Что это |
|---|---|

| `Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.CodeCoverage` + `.Msi` | Полноценная VSIX/MSI-часть coverage для **IDE** (UI, интеграция с Test Explorer). |
| `Microsoft.VisualStudio.PackageGroup.TestTools.CodeCoverage` | Группа, которая выбирает подмножество по продукту: IDE получает полный набор, Build Tools — только динамический движок + консоль. |
| `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.TestTools.BuildTools` | Компонент установки тестовых инструментов в Build Tools; тянет группу выше. |


  string(REPLACE "/INCREMENTAL" "" CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_DEBUG  "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_DEBUG}")

# === ПОСТРОИТЬ КОМАНДЫ КОМПИЛЯЦИИ И ЛИНКА ===
function(configure_target trgt PRODUCT_TARGET)
if(MSVC)
  # минимальная поддерживаемая ОС - win7 (и все дальнейшие)
  target_compile_definitions(${trgt} PRIVATE _WIN32_WINNT=0x0601)
  # в msvc /Zi, /EHsc, /DEBUG  будут дублироваться, но прописываются для ясности
  # target_compile_options - произвольные флаги компилятора 
  # PRIVATE даёт нетранзитивность: А (этот объект) и Б к нему сможет линковаться. а когда К линк. к Б, то К не будет линк. к А
  target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:/EHsc> /W4 /permissive-)

  # сюда будет заходить только для программ из задач, не для программ для тестирования (run_case, check) - им эти флаги не нужны
  if(PRODUCT_TARGET)
    # CMake проставит след. флаги автоматиечки: /Od (на release /O2 /Ob2); /MDd /MD; /DNDEBUG
    target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>:/Zi /fsanitize=address> $<$<CONFIG:Release>:/Zi>)
    target_link_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>:/DEBUG> $<$<CONFIG:Release>:/DEBUG /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF>)
  endif()

else()
  target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  # и в ветке продуктов, и в ветке тестовых программ оптимизация на релизе будет именно -O2, а не cmake-default -O3
  if (PRODUCT_TARGET) 
    # -O0 на дебаге будет подтянут CMake автоматически, а на релизе -DNDEBUG
    target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>: -g -fsanitize=address> $<$<CONFIG:Release>: -g -O2>)
    target_link_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Debug>: -fsanitize=address>)
  else()
    target_compile_options(${trgt} PRIVATE $<$<CONFIG:Release>: -O2>)
  endif()
endif()
endfunction()


# === Ф-ЦИЯ ДОБАВЛЕНИЯ ЗАДАЧИ === 
# сборки exe из main.c/main.cpp; уходит в каталог build/cfg/dir
function(add_task dir trgt src lib)
  # добавление исполняемного файла 
  # цель и её исходник. цель имеет одно имя (логическое, типа t1_c), а сделанный ею файл - другое (OUTPUT_NAME main)
  add_executable(${trgt} ${src})

  # в CMAKE_BINARY_DIR будет тот каталог, который был передан по -B
  set_target_properties(${trgt} PROPERTIES
  OUTPUT_NAME main
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${dir})

  # с кем линкуемся
  # тут private не имеет смысла (.exe конечен, к нему не линкуются), просто для единообразия
  target_link_libraries(${trgt} PRIVATE ${lib})

  # определение типа библиотеки т.к. на windows для .dll нужно доп. действие для связки с .exe
  get_target_property(lib_type ${lib} TYPE)
  # копирование dll в папку к exe даже если сам exe не перестраивался
  if(WIN32 AND lib_type STREQUAL "SHARED_LIBRARY")
    set(copied_dll "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${dir}/${lib}.dll")
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${copied_dll}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different $<TARGET_FILE:${lib}> "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${dir}"

# версии компонентов - минимальные (если есть) и на которых тестировали
# для компонентов, у которых actual проходит to_major_minor (компилятор, CMake, Ninja, git),
# значения в *_MIN / *_TESTED — в формате major.minor ("19.51", "4.3;4.2"): членство в списке точное

set(TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_TESTED "18.7")
set(TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_MIN "18.0")

# ф-ция cреза всего после major_minor: "19.51.36247.0" -> "19.51"; "4.3.1-msvc1" -> "4.3"; "1.13.2" -> "1.13"
function(to_major_minor out in)
  string(REGEX MATCH "^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+" matched "${in}")
  set(${out} "${matched}" PARENT_SCOPE)
endfunction()

# версия компонента проверяется и происходит падение/предупреждение/сообщение в зависимости от версии
function(check_component name actual tested min)
  if(NOT min STREQUAL "0" AND actual VERSION_LESS min)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "${name} ${actual} is older than minimal ${min}. upgrade the version")
  else()
    list(FIND tested "${actual}" _tested_idx)
    if(NOT _tested_idx EQUAL -1)
      # когда actual входит в список проверенных
      message(STATUS "${name} ${actual} is one of tested ${tested}")
    else()
      message(WARNING "${name} ${actual} is not one of tested ${tested}")
    endif()
  endif()
endfunction()

## Блокеры в текущем коде

1. **`NOT EXISTS MICROSOFT_COVERAGE` — ошибка.**  
   В CMake `EXISTS` не разыменовывает переменную: `NOT EXISTS MICROSOFT_COVERAGE` проверяет файл с буквальным именем `MICROSOFT_COVERAGE` в текущем каталоге. Условие будет истинным даже когда инструмент найден, и конфиг упадёт.  
   Нужно:
   ```cmake
   if(NOT MICROSOFT_COVERAGE OR NOT EXISTS "${MICROSOFT_COVERAGE}")
   ```
   Путь содержит пробелы (`Program Files (x86)`), поэтому кавычки обязательны.

2. **Проверка версии не подключена.**  
   `TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_TESTED` / `_MIN` добавлены, но нигде не используются. После `find_program` нужно:
   ```cmake
   execute_process(
     COMMAND "${MICROSOFT_COVERAGE}" --version
     OUTPUT_VARIABLE _coverage_raw
     OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
     RESULT_VARIABLE _coverage_rc)
   if(_coverage_rc STREQUAL "0")
     to_major_minor(_coverage_ver "${_coverage_raw}")
     check_component(CodeCoverage "${_coverage_ver}"
       "${TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_TESTED}" "${TOOLCHAIN_CODECOVERAGE_MIN}")
   else()
     message(WARNING "could not determine Microsoft.CodeCoverage.Console version "
       "(result: ${_coverage_rc}); version check skipped")
   endif()
   ```
   Сейчас `18.0` как MIN подтверждён каталогом, но код этого ещё не проверяет.

- **Компонент установки в README.** Coverage в Build Tools — опциональный компонент `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.TestTools.BuildTools`, а не часть workload `MSBuildTools`. На чистой машине без него `find_program` не найдёт инструмент. Это надо явно написать в инструкции установки окружения.
- **Сообщение об ошибке `find_program`.** Сейчас «Install it» — недостаточно: инструмент может быть установлен, но не быть в `PATH` обычного shell. Нужно подсказать: запускать из x64 Native Tools / Developer Prompt, либо добавить путь в `PATH`, либо доустановить компонент.
- **`cmake/coverage.settings.xml`.** Нет фильтрации отчёта: `Sources`/`ModulePaths`, исключение `tests/`, gtest/boost/vcpkg, `CollectFromChildProcesses=True`, `IncludeTestAssembly` по необходимости. Без этого в отчёт попадут тесты и сторонний код.
